audit.whatIsWrong: diff was 'HARD' while diffRating is 4/10, breakdown.difficulty says 4/10 and report[14] says 'Favoured matchup' at a 53.1% win rate. Level 1 was marked Jax in both layers although whys[0] says 'Level 1 is even', and First item was marked Skill although whys[5] and spikes[2] describe it as Jax's forcing window.
audit.why: Packet levelChart is Skill / Jax / Jax / Jax / Jax / Jax / Nasus. The mirror (nasus__jax) set its own side to EVEN 6/10, which inverts to 4/10 favoured for Jax — the enum was the only thing out of step.
audit.corrected: diff FAV; phases[0]/win[0] Skill; phases[5]/win[5] Jax with rating raised. Chart rows proposed as matched pairs.

audit.whatIsWrong: Repeated claim that Wither is 'locked behind level 6' / 'does not exist until 6' (whys[3], early, mid). Wither is Nasus's W — available from level 2, 15/14/13/12/11s cooldown.
audit.why: This is the single most load-bearing error on the page: it tells a Jax player he has a free window from 3 to 5 that does not exist. Nasus's actual level-6 spike is Fury of the Sands (120/100/80s), which gives health, range, resists and a reduced Siphoning Strike cooldown.
audit.corrected: Wither described at its real availability (level 2+, 15s at rank 1); level 6 reassigned to Fury of the Sands.

audit.whatIsWrong: Jax's ultimate written as 'Grandmaster at Arms' in whys[4] and spikes[1].text. Riot's kit names it Grandmaster's Might.
audit.why: Fabricated ability name, and the same one the mirror flagged. The decisive interaction also needed stating: Counter Strike dodges basic attacks, and Siphoning Strike is an auto-attack reset — so Nasus's empowered swing IS an auto and Counter Strike does dodge it, which is exactly why the E-into-recast pattern works here.
audit.corrected: Grandmaster's Might used; whys[2] now states that Siphoning Strike is an auto reset and therefore dodgeable by Counter Strike.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown numbers anywhere in the trading advice.
audit.why: Wither is 15s at rank 1 and Counter Strike is 17s at rank 1 — Jax's stun is on a longer cooldown than Nasus's kite early, which is the real reason not to burn E on chip.
audit.corrected: Level 2 phase why now carries both numbers.

edits.before: Counter Strike flips every AA exchange he starts. Only take the trade when Nasus's Wither is down.
edits.after: Wither is up from level 2 on a 15s cooldown and your E is 17s — bait the slow, then trade.

edits.before: Grandmaster’s Might stats win every extended duel from here on. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Nasus's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Grandmaster's Might out-stats him, but Fury of the Sands gives him health, range and resists — all-in only with your active up.

edits.before: Counter Strike dodges his committal Q-auto and stuns him, and Leap Strike sticks him for the full combo he cannot escape.
edits.after: Siphoning Strike is an auto reset, so Counter Strike dodges his committal swing outright and stuns, and Leap Strike sticks him for the full combo.

edits.before: You out-trade a pre-6 Nasus — bait the Empowered Q into your E and grind him while his Wither is still locked behind level 6.
edits.after: You out-trade a pre-6 Nasus — bait the Empowered Q into your E and grind him in the 15s window while Wither is on cooldown.

edits.before: Grandmaster at Arms' Armor/MR active and every-third-hit magic on-hit turn a Wither-slowed trade into a clean kill.
edits.after: Grandmaster's Might's Armor/MR active and every-third-hit magic on-hit turn a Wither-slowed trade into a clean kill.

edits.before: Grandmaster at Arms: the Armor/MR active plus the every-third-hit magic on-hit turns a Wither-slowed trade into a kill, since his only answer is a single stacked Q and a slow walk-up.
edits.after: Grandmaster's Might: the Armor/MR active plus the every-third-hit magic on-hit turns a Wither-slowed trade into a kill, but Fury of the Sands adds health, range and resists — force it while his R is down.

edits.before: Level 1 is a non-event for the trade — you have no Counter Strike yet and neither does he, so just contest last-hits and make sure his Q never lands a free-stack cannon minion. Counter Strike unlocks at 3, and that is when the lane becomes yours: when he winds up an Empowered Q to last-hit, pop E to dodge the swing and the autos, recast to stun, and Leap Strike in for a trade he cannot answer — Wither does not exist until 6. Every stack you deny is starving the only thing that makes him scary later.
edits.after: Level 1 is a non-event for the trade — you have no Counter Strike yet and neither does he, so just contest last-hits and make sure his Q never lands a free-stack cannon minion. Counter Strike unlocks at 3, and that is when the lane becomes yours: when he winds up an Empowered Q to last-hit, pop E to dodge the swing (Siphoning Strike is an auto reset, so it is dodgeable), recast to stun, and Leap Strike in. Wither is up from 2, so start the trade only once he has spent it or is out of its 700 range.

edits.before: This is your takeover window. His whole trade is one big stacked Q plus an auto, so bait it into Counter Strike, dodge it, stun, and grind him down with your passive's attack-speed ramp and every-third-hit magic. The one thing to respect is Wither — once it lands at 6 your attack speed and movement crater, so save E to dodge the Q he throws while you are slowed, or just disengage with Leap Strike off a minion. At 6 your R's Armor/MR active flips a Wither trade into a kill; this is the moment to force the all-in and put him behind on stacks.
edits.after: This is your takeover window. His whole trade is one big stacked Q plus an auto, so bait it into Counter Strike, dodge it, stun, and grind him down with your passive's attack-speed ramp and every-third-hit magic. The one thing to respect is Wither — it lands your attack speed and movement crater for its duration, so save E to dodge the Q he throws while slowed, or disengage with Leap Strike off a minion. Its 15s cooldown is your window. At 6 your R's Armor/MR active flips a Wither trade into a kill; force the all-in and put him behind on stacks.

notes: The page told Jax players that Wither 'does not exist until 6' in three separate fields. Wither is Nasus's W, live from level 2 on a 15/14/13/12/11s cooldown — the false free window would have got players killed walking into a slow they thought was unavailable. Nasus's level-6 spike is Fury of the Sands. Also re-fixed the 'Grandmaster at Arms' name the mirror flagged. Confirming the mirror's note: champ-data/_kits/jax.json carries a 'dash' flag on Empower (W) that is a parsing artifact — Empower is a bonus-damage auto reset with no movement; nothing here was written from it.
